mobile_ap.executive_summary: This week's material lacks substantive technical or competitive moves in mobile AP design, packaging, or protocol boundaries. The Apple health study signals compute capability relevance but remains research-stage; the India laptop survey confirms Snapdragon's market share momentum but offers no new architectural or yield data. No change to competitive standings.

foundry.executive_summary: NVIDIA's CEO transition injects supply-chain recalculation risk into the foundry ecosystem; Samsung gains tactical negotiating room with TSMC while SK Hynix doubles down on HBM4 packaging and test capacity despite AI sector uncertainty, signaling that memory-interface integration—not core logic—remains the competitive vector. TSMC's public logic-only posture is now shadowed by rival capital deployment aimed explicitly at packaging and assembly nodes where margin and control concentrate.

packaging.executive_summary: Packaging ecosystem consolidates around dual momentum: TSMC-Xintec seven-year CoWoS capacity deal (through 2033) anchors AI/HBM supply guarantees, while Daxin Materials' semiconductor revenue breakthrough (22.7%, first time >20%) and Taiwan APS Holdings' ceramic substrate IPO (NT$188/share) signal materials-layer commoditization is reversing through platform differentiation. Chiplet standardization (UCIe 4.0 memory integration, Imec-ASRA automotive ACIR specs) now creates vertical lock-in at the interposer boundary, favoring integrated materials players over standalone interconnect vendors.

hbm.executive_summary: Samsung and SK Hynix are consolidating HBM packaging and test dominance while simultaneously capturing custom base-die production via platform-locked partnerships—Samsung now holds HBM4E for Meta on 2nm (outsourcing commodity logic, not packaging), while SK Hynix aggressively scales HBM4 capacity for H1 2025 operations. The tactical inversion is now complete: Korean suppliers own the packaging-interposer boundary (high-margin, differentiation point), while hyperscalers (Google, Meta) are systematizing direct HBM procurement to bypass Broadcom intermediation and lock packaging specs to their own base-die roadmaps, fragmenting the previously unified HBM ecosystem into platform-specific supply chains.

pmic.executive_summary: No material shift in PMIC supply dynamics this week. MaxLinear's new AI optics power chip launch addresses application-layer demand but does not alter underlying BCD/mature-node capacity allocation or pricing pressure from Chinese competitors (SMIC, Hua Hong). TSMC/Samsung's continued 8-inch capacity reduction remains the structural driver; Chinese matnode producers remain positioned to capture volume-based cost advantage.
